rejected.reason: The definition of 'Riot' requires collective violent unrest; frames f4–f6 show a tense standoff between police in riot gear and civilians holding flags, but no violence, destruction, or chaotic collective action is visible. This constitutes a protest or confrontation, not a riot. Frames f7–f10 are too degraded (overexposed, occluded, ground-level) to support any category. No evidence of violence meets the required threshold.

The frames show a crowd gathered around a white SUV with open doors and people standing nearby, but no collective violent unrest, property destruction, or aggressive group behavior is visible; the scene is consistent with a public gathering or incident response without rioting.

Crowd movement and presence of flags/chanting are visible, but no collective violent unrest (e.g., property destruction, attacks on persons or vehicles) is observed; the scene remains orderly with people walking and standing.
The white vehicle behind the sedan appears to be parked or slowly maneuvering; no impact, deformation, skid marks, or sudden motion indicating a crash is visible in f8–f9.
In f18–f20, individuals are near each other but no mutual physical combat (grappling, striking) is visible; movements appear consistent with walking through a crowd.
